review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

5:1.sourceText: Πρεσβυτέρῳ μὴ ἐπιπλήξῃς, ἀλλὰ παρακάλει ὡς πατέρα, νεωτέρους ὡς ἀδελφούς,
5:1.targetText: You may not rebuke an elder, but exhort [him] as a father, younger persons as brothers,

groups.note: The actual elder, Πρεσβυτέρῳ, is the person not to rebuke and also the understood object of the contrasting exhort predicate. English repeats that same person as bracketed him; the dative elder identity is retained across both expressions without inventing a source pronoun.

5:2.sourceText: πρεσβυτέρας ὡς μητέρας, νεωτέρας ὡς ἀδελφὰς ἐν πάσῃ ἁγνείᾳ.
5:2.targetText: aged women as mothers, younger ones as sisters—in all purity;

5:3.targetText: honor widows who are really widows;

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies are in the nominal widows-who-are-really-widows description. Greek has the article/adverb/noun phrase without a finite be verb or being participle.

5:4.sourceText: εἰ δέ τις χήρα τέκνα ἢ ἔκγονα ἔχει, μανθανέτωσαν πρῶτον τὸν ἴδιον οἶκον εὐσεβεῖν καὶ ἀμοιβὰς ἀποδιδόναι τοῖς προγόνοις· τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ἀπόδεκτον ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ.
5:4.targetText: and if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to show piety to their own house, and to give back a repayment to the parents, for this is right and acceptable before God.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.
The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness phrase addition: LSV right and before acceptable follows TR καλὸν καί; pinned N1904 has only acceptable here.

5:5.sourceText: ἡ δὲ ὄντως χήρα καὶ μεμονωμένη ἤλπικεν ἐπὶ Θεὸν καὶ προσμένει ταῖς δεήσεσιν καὶ ταῖς προσευχαῖς νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας·
5:5.targetText: And she who is really a widow and desolate, has hoped on God, and remains in the supplications and in the prayers night and day,

groups.note: The perfect passive μεμονωμένη describes having been left alone; LSV expresses the resulting state as desolate without a separate auxiliary at that participle.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies is in the really-a-widow nominal description; no finite copula is written there. The following actual perfect being-left-alone participle is separately rendered desolate.

5:6.targetText: but she given to luxury [while] living has died;

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English while makes the temporal relation of the living participle explicit; pinned N1904 has no separate while conjunction.

5:7.sourceText: καὶ ταῦτα παράγγελλε, ἵνα ἀνεπίλημπτοι ὦσιν.
5:7.targetText: and charge these things, that they may be blameless;

5:8.sourceText: εἰ δέ τις τῶν ἰδίων καὶ μάλιστα οἰκείων οὐ προνοεῖ, τὴν πίστιν ἤρνηται καὶ ἔστιν ἀπίστου χείρων.
5:8.targetText: and if anyone does not provide for his own, and especially for those of the household, he has denied the faith, and he is worse than an unbeliever.

groups.note: The substantival οἰκείων designates members of one’s household, genitive complement of provide; English for those of the household spells out that family designation without additional Greek those/household tokens.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

5:9.sourceText: Χήρα καταλεγέσθω μὴ ἔλαττον ἐτῶν ἑξήκοντα γεγονυῖα, ἑνὸς ἀνδρὸς γυνή,
5:9.targetText: A widow—do not let her be enrolled under sixty years of age, having been a wife of one husband,

groups.note: Greek less with the preceding μή gives not less than sixty; LSV renders the age limit as do not enroll under sixty. The less/under threshold word is retained within that negative scope.

The participle γεγονυῖα follows the sixty-years phrase and precedes wife. It can complete the age qualification, having reached sixty, or be associated with the wife description; LSV explicitly renders having been a wife. The actual being/becoming head is preserved without pretending that this syntactic attachment is uniquely determined by the word alone.

5:10.sourceText: ἐν ἔργοις καλοῖς μαρτυρουμένη, εἰ ἐτεκνοτρόφησεν, εἰ ἐξενοδόχησεν, εἰ ἁγίων πόδας ἔνιψεν, εἰ θλιβομένοις ἐπήρκεσεν, εἰ παντὶ ἔργῳ ἀγαθῷ ἐπηκολούθησεν.
5:10.targetText: being testified to in good works: if she brought up children, if she entertained strangers, if she washed holy ones’ feet, if she relieved those in tribulation, if she followed after every good work;

review.note: The child-rearing and stranger-hospitality compounds are each rendered as full English verb/object phrases. Those lexical child/stranger components belong to their actual compound verbs, not invented separate Greek nouns.

5:11.sourceText: νεωτέρας δὲ χήρας παραιτοῦ· ὅταν γὰρ καταστρηνιάσωσιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, γαμεῖν θέλουσιν,
5:11.targetText: and be refusing younger widows, for when they may revel against the Christ, they wish to marry,

groups.note: The compound καταστρηνιάσωσιν with the genitive Christ denotes luxurious/desire-driven rejection against Christ, rendered revel against. The English against expresses that actual compound/complement relation without an independent Greek against preposition.

5:12.sourceText: ἔχουσαι κρίμα ὅτι τὴν πρώτην πίστιν ἠθέτησαν·
5:12.targetText: having judgment, because they cast away the first faith,

5:13.sourceText: ἅμα δὲ καὶ ἀργαὶ μανθάνουσιν, περιερχόμεναι τὰς οἰκίας, οὐ μόνον δὲ ἀργαὶ ἀλλὰ καὶ φλύαροι καὶ περίεργοι, λαλοῦσαι τὰ μὴ δέοντα.
5:13.targetText: and also at the same time, they learn [to be] idle, going around the houses; and not only idle, but also tattlers and busybodies, speaking things they should not;

groups.note: The substantival obligation participle δέοντα, things fitting/required, is recast as the English relative-modal description things they should not speak. They is the understood speakers, not a separate Greek pronoun.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English to be completes learn idle; pinned N1904 has no separate being infinitive.

5:14.sourceText: βούλομαι οὖν νεωτέρας γαμεῖν, τεκνογονεῖν, οἰκοδεσποτεῖν, μηδεμίαν ἀφορμὴν διδόναι τῷ ἀντικειμένῳ λοιδορίας χάριν·
5:14.targetText: I intend, therefore, younger ones to marry, to bear children, to be mistress of the house, to give no occasion to the opposer of reviling;

targetPhrases.text: to be mistress of the house

groups.note: The household-mastering verb οἰκοδεσποτεῖν means manage a household; LSV expands it as to be mistress of the house for the younger women. No separate Greek be, mistress or house noun is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: The postposition χάριν marks the purpose for the sake of reviling; LSV uses the nominal occasion of reviling relation without a separate purpose connector.

5:15.sourceText: ἤδη γάρ τινες ἐξετράπησαν ὀπίσω τοῦ Σατανᾶ.
5:15.targetText: for some already turned aside after Satan.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

5:16.sourceText: εἴ τις πιστὴ ἔχει χήρας, ἐπαρκείτω αὐταῖς, καὶ μὴ βαρείσθω ἡ ἐκκλησία, ἵνα ταῖς ὄντως χήραις ἐπαρκέσῃ.
5:16.targetText: If any believing man or believing woman has widows, let them relieve them, and do not let the assembly be burdened, that it may relieve those [who are] really widows.

groups.note: The actual feminine believing adjective πιστή designates a believing woman. LSV’s added male alternative comes from the longer TR reading and is separately unpaired, not assigned to this feminine source identity.

The written third-person imperative is singular, let her relieve, governed by N1904 any believing woman. LSV uses them under its wider man-or-woman subject; the same relief action is retained with that subject/number wording difference explicit.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness subject addition: the additional TR πιστὸς ἤ introduces a believing man or before believing woman. Pinned N1904 has only the feminine πιστή.
Bracketed English relative/copula supplies the nominal those-really-widows description; the actual Greek article supplies those only, without a being verb.

5:17.sourceText: Οἱ καλῶς προεστῶτες πρεσβύτεροι διπλῆς τιμῆς ἀξιούσθωσαν, μάλιστα οἱ κοπιῶντες ἐν λόγῳ καὶ διδασκαλίᾳ.
5:17.targetText: Let them, the well-leading elders, be counted worthy of double honor, especially those laboring in word and teaching,

5:18.sourceText: λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή Βοῦν ἀλοῶντα οὐ φιμώσεις, καί Ἄξιος ὁ ἐργάτης τοῦ μισθοῦ αὐτοῦ.
5:18.targetText: for the Writing says, “You will not muzzle an ox treading out,” and, “Worthy [is] the workman of his reward.”

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

5:19.sourceText: κατὰ πρεσβυτέρου κατηγορίαν μὴ παραδέχου, ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ ἐπὶ δύο ἢ τριῶν μαρτύρων.
5:19.targetText: Do not receive an accusation against an elder, except on two or three witnesses.

groups.note: The exception idiom ἐκτὸς εἰ μή, except unless, is rendered as the single English except; its written negative belongs to the exception construction, not a second English not.

5:20.sourceText: Τοὺς ἁμαρτάνοντας ἐνώπιον πάντων ἔλεγχε, ἵνα καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ φόβον ἔχωσιν.
5:20.targetText: Reprove those sinning before all, that the others may also have fear;

5:21.sourceText: διαμαρτύρομαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν ἀγγέλων ἵνα ταῦτα φυλάξῃς χωρὶς προκρίματος, μηδὲν ποιῶν κατὰ πρόσκλισιν.
5:21.targetText: I fully testify, before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the chosen messengers, that you may keep these things, without prejudging, doing nothing by partiality.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness title addition: LSV the Lord follows TR κυρίου, absent from pinned N1904 Christ Jesus. The actual Christ and Jesus title/name remain linked despite reversed English order.

5:22.sourceText: Χεῖρας ταχέως μηδενὶ ἐπιτίθει, μηδὲ κοινώνει ἁμαρτίαις ἀλλοτρίαις· σεαυτὸν ἁγνὸν τήρει.
5:22.targetText: Be quickly laying hands on no one, nor be having fellowship with [the] sins of others; be keeping yourself pure;

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English definite article is supplied before anarthrous Greek sins; no Greek article is written here.

5:23.sourceText: Μηκέτι ὑδροπότει, ἀλλὰ οἴνῳ ὀλίγῳ χρῶ διὰ τὸν στόμαχον καὶ τὰς πυκνάς σου ἀσθενείας.
5:23.targetText: no longer be drinking water, but be using a little wine, because of your stomach and of your frequent sicknesses;

groups.note: The single causal διά governs both stomach and sicknesses; English repeats the causal of at the second coordinated reason. Both English relation pieces retain that one written source preposition.

The Greek definite article/body-part phrase identifies the addressed person’s stomach; English uses possessive your stomach for that contextual body-part designation. This is not a separate source your pronoun, and the actual later σου belongs to the sicknesses.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

5:24.sourceText: Τινῶν ἀνθρώπων αἱ ἁμαρτίαι πρόδηλοί εἰσιν προάγουσαι εἰς κρίσιν, τισὶν δὲ καὶ ἐπακολουθοῦσιν·
5:24.targetText: the sins of certain men are evident beforehand, leading before to judgment, but some also they follow after;

groups.note: The dative some identifies the people whom the sins follow, rendered some also they follow after; it is not the subject pronoun they, which is encoded in the following verb for the sins.

5:25.sourceText: ὡσαύτως καὶ τὰ ἔργα τὰ καλὰ πρόδηλα, καὶ τὰ ἄλλως ἔχοντα κρυβῆναι οὐ δύνανται.
5:25.targetText: in like manner the right works are also evident beforehand, and those that are otherwise are not able to be hid.

groups.note: The present having/being participle ἔχοντα with otherwise describes things in a different condition; LSV recasts the predicate as are otherwise. That actual participle supports are, while the article stays with those that.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV supplies are in the right-works-evident nominal predicate; TR explicitly has ἐστιν, absent from pinned N1904. This first are is not assigned to the article or borrowed from the later having participle.
